title: Member Services Policy: PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) on More Than One Service Account
content:
**Section 1. Several enrollments per member.** A member may run PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) on more than one service account (a home and a shop, for example). Each enrollment is its own prepay account with its own prepaid balance, its own arrears balance and its own alerts. This policy sets no maximum number of PrePay Power enrollments one member may hold.

**Section 2. One enrollment per service account at a time.** A service account may carry only one enrollment at a time. A service account that already has a PrePay Power account awaiting activation, active, or disconnected for low balance cannot be enrolled again.

**Section 3. Separation of accounts.** Payments, alerts and disconnections of one prepay account never touch another.

**Section 4. Basis of the check.** Whether a service account already carries an enrollment is read from the cooperative's PrePay Power account records for that same service account and their status, not from the member's account of it. A new enrollment is always a separate prepay account record.

### Status of an existing PrePay Power account on the same service account

| Status of the existing account | New enrollment of that service account |
|---|---|
| awaiting activation | cannot be taken |
| active | cannot be taken |
| disconnected for low balance | cannot be taken |

### Illustrations (hypothetical holdings)

- A member holds an active PrePay Power account on a home meter and asks to enroll a shop meter that has no PrePay Power account: the shop meter is a different service account, so Section 2 does not stand in the way, and the two enrollments keep separate balances and alerts.
- A payment made to the shop enrollment raises only the shop's prepaid balance; a disconnection of the home meter for low balance does not affect the shop enrollment.
